newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-THREE TIED FOR SENIOR TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP LEAD, IRWIN FADES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THREE TIED FOR SENIOR TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP LEAD, IRWIN FADES.

text.p: Tour money leader Hale Irwin soared to a 75 Friday and Vicente Fernandez, Jay Sigel and Frank Conner took advantage to share the lead after 36 holes of the $1.6 million Senior Tour Championship.

Fernandez, who began the day one shot behind Irwin, shot a two-under-par 70 to move to six-under 138 at The Dunes. Conner fired a 67 and Sigel carded his second consecutive 69 to surge into a tie for the lead.
Fernandez had a bogey-free round, sinking birdie putts on the 10th and 11th holes from eight and nine feet out.

Sigel started his round with a bogey on the first hole, but finished with a flourish. He sank a 20-foot birdie putt on 14, and then eagled 15, where he hit a 2-iron to within 14 feet. He completed his round with a birdie from 25 feet at 18.
Conner also bogeyed the first hole before catching fire and posting six birdies for the low round of the day.

Mike Hill and 60-year-old Bob Charles of New Zealand, one of the shortest hitters on Tour, were tied for fourth at 139. Hill posted a 70 and Charles, who captured the Kaanapali Classic two weeks ago, shot 71.
Defending champion Jim Colbert, who leads the Tour with five wins this year and is chasing Irwin for the money title, was alone in sixth place at four-under 140 after shooting 70.
John Bland, who has won four times this season, was one shot further back at 141, with Irwin, Gary Player and Raymond Floyd knotted at 142.
Lee Trevino, who won a record five-way playoff last week at the Emerald Coast Classic, shot 73 to stand at 143.
The top 31 players on the Tour money list are playing in this season-ending event, which delivers $280,000 to the winner.
